title: The inner union of Abba and Ima: Shabbos, new souls and Moshiach
overview:
Chapter 26 brings the descent of the light into *Abba* and *Ima* themselves. They unite in two ways. The inner union, for their own sake, is *chachma* and *bina* looking at their own depth and higher, to *Atik*: it is the light of Shabbos, and it comes from the *mazalos* of *Arich*. The outer union is *chachma* turned to the *middos*, the *vav ketzavos* and the *Nehi* of *Abba*: deciding guilty or innocent, as in most learning of the *Talmud*, or just applying what one already knows. Most people never go past this; they live on axioms they were handed.

The inner union comes only through *hisbonenus* with *mesirus nefesh*, the *mesirus nefesh* of the Shema, and only it brings new births: new *middos*, new souls, and Moshiach, who cannot come otherwise. The *mashal* is a wondrous sage, who knows an idea at its source and so can recast it for a small child and bring new ideas out of it. That is why the union that brings souls is on Friday night.

terms.gloss: the inner side: the intellect looking into itself, and higher than itself
the outer side: the intellect turned to the middos, as in deciding guilty or innocent
the six directions: the middos of chachma (or bina), the thinking about whether it should be chesed or gevura
firm in his mind: the strength of Nehi, like legs holding up the body; its opposite is the wishy-washy guy
an intellectual axiom: the way things lie in one's head, taken for granted; what most people think from
the fiftieth gate: bina sheb'bina when it goes past the depth of bina and chachma, to Atik and higher
self-sacrifice; here the real hisbonenus, given over into the Atzmus, which brings the inner union
lit. Israel the elder: with tevuna, the lower Abba and Ima, the vav ketzavos, which spread outward to bring out the middos
the mazalos of Arich, chachma stima'a and bina stima'a: the root the inner union receives from, without which there is no birth
an offspring: a new birth, of middos, of souls or of an idea
G-d most high: the ascent of the inner light of Abba when it receives from the mazal
a wondrous sage, "a super smart guy", who knows an idea in its inner quarry and so can explain it to a child and bring new ideas out of it

sections.title: Shabbos and Yom Tov: the inner union of Abba and Ima
sections.summary: The light now comes down within the ten *sefiros* of *Abba* and *Ima* themselves. Their inner side, the *ayin* of *chachma* and the depth of *bina* united, is the light of Shabbos and Yom Tov.

phrases.he: (כו) ומעתה יש להבין בירידת האור עוד בעשר ספירות דאבא ואמא עצמן
מבחינת פנימית המוחין דאבא ואמא כשהן מקבלים מחסד וגבורה דאריך אנפין
ומכל שכן כשעולין לקבל ממזלות דאריך אנפין כנזכר לעיל
לבחינת חיצונית נה''י דאבא ואמא שמלובשין במוחין דזעיר אנפין, וכמו שכתוב בעץ חיים.

skip.note: Read straight through at the opening of the tape, with no English and no comment.

phrases.he: והענין ידוע כמו שבת ויום טוב, הן בבחינת פנימית המוחין דאבא ואמא
כי השבת נקרא קודש בעונג, דחכמה
מלה בגרמיה
phrases.en: a thing unto itself

phrases.he: והוא בחינת פנימית אור אבא (שהוא פנימית עתיק יומין, וזה שנאמר וקראת לשבת עונג, וכמו שכתוב במקום אחר בענין ג' סעודות דשבת באריכות)
ויום טוב נקרא מקרא קדש, בחינת שמחה,
כמו שכתוב אם הבנים שמחה
שהוא בחינת מוחין דאימא שמקבל מאבא, כי השביתה דשבת הוא בחכמה גם כן

blocks.text: Shabbos and Yom Tov come from the *pnimiyus* (inner side) of the *mochin* (intellect) of *Abba* and *Ima*. Shabbos is holy and delight, the delight of *chachma*, which is *milsa bigarmei*, **a thing unto itself**: the inner light of *Abba*, the inner side of *Atik Yomin*. Yom Tov is a calling of holiness and joy, the *mochin* of *Ima*, which receives from *Abba*.

phrases.he: דהיינו בפנימית אבא, בחינת כח מה
אין דחכמה קודם שמתפשט ליש בהשגה דבינה
וכן בינה בבחינת פנימית, הוא עומק נקודת המושג כו', כידוע שיש אין חכמה בבינה ובינה בחכמה
והיינו הבן בחכמה וחכם בבינה, שזהו בחינת יחוד פנימית דאבא ואמא

blocks.text: The inner side of *Abba* is the *koach MaH* (the power of what), the *ayin* (nothing) of *chachma* before it spreads into a *yesh* (something) in the grasp of *bina*. The inner side of *bina* is the depth of the point grasped, and there is *ayin* of *chachma* in *bina* and *bina* in *chachma*. "That's all in chapter one." This is the inner *yichud* (union) of *Abba* and *Ima*.

sections.title: The outer side: the middos of chachma, and how the Talmud is learned
sections.summary: Where *chachma* and *bina* look into *chesed* or *gevura*, guilty or innocent, they are only the outer side of the intellect, the *vav ketzavos* of *Abba*. Real intellect looks higher than intellect, and the *Talmud* itself can be learned that way.

phrases.he: מה שאין כן בחיצונית השפע דחכמה ובינה בחג''ת נה''י כו',
כמו מדות שבחכמה
phrases.en: the *chachma* of whether it should be *chesed* or *gevura*: that's called *chesed* and *gevura* of *chachma*

phrases.he: שנקרא בחינת ו׳ קצוות דאבא

blocks.text: Not so the outer side of the flow of *chachma* and *bina* into *Chagas* and *Nehi*. The *Chabad* of *chachma* and *bina* that is the inner *yichud* is when a person is actually doing *hisbonenus* (contemplation). As chapters one and two said, the whole of *Chabad* is powered by *bina sheb'bina*, analytical *hisbonenus*.

Real *hisbonenus* does not analyze things in this world, which are a matter of *middos*. Even the real *iyun* of the *Talmud* asks whether he is *chayav* or *zakai*, liable or innocent: *chesed* and *gevura*. It is *Chabad* of the *middos*, the *chitzoniyus* (outer side) of *iyun*, except for the really great sages, who learned the *Gemara* as its *pnimiyus*.

The real business of *sechel* is not looking into what the *midda* should be but into what is higher than the *sechel*, and that is obvious. Someone really smart asks, "What's really going on here?", not just how to make more money or get along better with his wife. That matters, but the real *yichud* of inner *chachma* and *bina* is pure *Chabad*: *Chabad* looking into *Chabad*, or *Kachab* (*Keser*, *chachma* and *bina*), not into the *middos*.

In the *Gemara* too, the real *iyun* is less into the *middos* of the case than into its real *taam* (reason) and *ratzon* (will). The *Talmud* is not a book of laws, as Reb Levik would learn it: it is a book of the *ratzon* of the *Aibershter* (G-d), His *ratzon* and *taanug* (delight). As the Rebbe Rashab said, *nigleh* (the revealed Torah) should be learned like *Chassidus*, and vice versa.

He rereads the line. Where the thinking is into the *middos*, then even though it is *chachma* and not *middos*, it is still the *middos* of *chachma*: **the *chachma* of whether it should be *chesed* or *gevura*** is called *chesed* and *gevura* of *chachma*, the *vav ketzavos* (six directions) of *Abba*.

phrases.he: כמו חסד שבחכמה,
דהיינו כח שכל המטה כלפי חסד
phrases.en: the *sechel* that *mateh klapei chesed*

phrases.he: או כח שכל אחר שמטה כלפי דין כו'
ומאירים בחסד וגבורה דבינה
phrases.en: *chesed* and *gevura* of *chachma* is *meir* in *chesed* and *gevura* of *bina*

phrases.he: דהוא בא בהשגה בטוב טעם בהסבר לזכות ולחוב
ונקרא מדות שבשכל המושג, קודם שנולדו במהות בפני עצמן
phrases.en: the *sechel* of *middos*, not a *midda* that is born into an actual *midda*: it's not a feeling yet

phrases.he: (כמו שיתבאר)

blocks.text: *Chesed* of *chachma* is **the *sechel* that *mateh klapei chesed***, leaning toward kindness; it is not looking into the inner side of reality. Another mind leans toward *din* (judgement). They shine into the *chesed* and *gevura* of *bina*, where it is grasped with good reason, to acquit or convict: the *Talmud*, its outer side anyway. These are **the *sechel* of *middos***, not yet a *midda* born: **it's not a feeling yet**.

phrases.he: וכאשר אינו מוצא טעם בהסבר השגה, ומכל מקום לא יוכל לומר בהיפוך כי שכלו מטה כך, היינו בבחינת חסד וגבורה דאבא קודם שמאיר מאין ליש בבינה (כמו ענין שתיק רב כו')
(והשתיקה סייג לחכמה,
משתוקא בתרין,
phrases.en: if words are worth one coin, silence is worth two

phrases.he: מפני שעולה ביטול כח מ''ה דחכמה זה למקור המוציא כל השכלות, שנקרא חכמה סתימאה כנזכר לעיל, ומוציא משם השכלה חדשה כו')

blocks.text: When he finds no reason to explain it and still cannot say the opposite, because his mind leans that way, that is *chesed* and *gevura* of *Abba*, before it shines from *ayin* to *yesh* in *bina*: Rav was silent. This is what he means: the *pilpulim* (debates) of the *Mishna* and the *Gemara*, which he calls here the *middos* of *chachma* and *bina*.

Silence is a fence for wisdom: *mishtuka bisrein*, **if words are worth one coin, silence is worth two**. Silence here does not just mean not talking. It is the inner *bittul* (self-nullification) of the mind, the *koach MaH* of *chachma* rising to the source that brings everything out, *chachma stima'a* (the hidden wisdom), and bringing something new out of it.

sections.title: Nehi of Abba: a firm mind, and the axioms most people live by
sections.summary: The third level of *chachma* is its *Nehi*: not deciding what should be, but bringing what one knows to bear, with a mind that stands firm on its legs. Most people's thinking never goes higher than this; it runs on axioms they were handed.

phrases.he: ובחינת נה''י דאבא, היינו בחינת מאזני השכל והחכמה, איך שיבא הדבר חכמה לידי השפעה בבחינת כליות יועצות כו'

blocks.text: *Nehi* of *Abba* are the scales of the intellect: how a matter of *chachma* comes to be given over. So *chachma* has three levels, which receive from the three levels in *Arich* spoken of before. The inner level is pure *hisbonenus*, *Chabad* within *chachma*. The second is also *hisbonenus*, called *iyun*, like the *iyun* of the *Gemara*: a *hisbonenus* into the *middos*.

The third is a *hisbonenus* not into which *midda* it should be but into how the *sechel* should come to be given over. You are not trying to figure out the *halacha*: you know it, a book told you, and you try to apply it, bring it out, or teach it to somebody.

phrases.he: (והיינו ענין התוקף שיש במוח, שנקרא תקיף בדעתו
כמו הרגלים שיש בהן כח להקים כל הגוף, כך בחינת נצח והוד דאבא מקימין לגוף המוחין
ולהיפוך כשאינו תקיף בדעתו, בקל יפול מסברתו מחוב לזכות
phrases.en: He's a wishy-washy guy: one day you'll convince him one way, and the next day you'll convince him another way

phrases.he: ומטמא לטהור כו'
וכן בנצח והוד דאמא)
phrases.en: That's also the strength of the *bina*

blocks.text: This is the *tokef* (strength) in the mind, called *takif b'daito* (firm in his mind). *Nehi* in general is strength, as you say a guy has guts. The legs, also called *netzach* and *hod*, have the power to hold up the whole body; so *netzach* and *hod* of *Abba* hold up the body of the *mochin*.

Someone not firm in his mind falls easily from guilty to innocent. **He's a wishy-washy guy** with no strong *Nehi*: **one day you'll convince him one way, and the next day you'll convince him another way**. *Netzach* and *hod* of *Ima* are likewise the strength of *bina*.

phrases.he: ודרך כלל,
phrases.en: and in general

phrases.he: הרי רק מבחינת נה''י דאבא שמלובשים בנה''י דאימא, משם נמצא מקור המוחין לזעיר אנפין,
שהן בחינת המדות שלמטה מן השכל (כמו שיתבאר)

blocks.text: **And in general**, the source of the *mochin* of *Zeir Anpin*, the *middos* below the intellect, is only the *Nehi* of *Abba* dressed in the *Nehi* of *Ima*; and *Abba* and *Ima* themselves usually receive only from the *Nehi* of *Arich*. A person is not really looking into what the *middos* should be, and certainly not into what the whole thing is about.

In everything they do, people mostly receive only from the *Nehi* of *Abba*: from the *hanacha sichlis* they already have, the way things lie in their heads. There has to be an English word for it; translated exactly, it is an intellectual axiom.

blocks.title: Save the whales
blocks.text: By them it is axiomatic: you've got to save the whales. They are not asking whether you really should, still less how whales came into being in the first place, only what to do now: raise money, make brochures. What the *middos* should be is already settled for them.

sensitivity.reason: Uses a present-day activist cause as the example of an unexamined axiom; a reader in that cause could take it as a jab.
sensitivity.publishable: By them it is axiomatic: you've got to support a certain cause. They are not asking whether you really should, still less how the thing came into being in the first place, only what to do now: raise money, make brochures. What the *middos* should be is already settled for them.
sensitivity.judgmentNote: The whales are a mild, almost neutral example and the point does not depend on them; it may well print raw.

blocks.text: So when did they think it through, to arrive at the axiom? Most people didn't. It was given to them; they just got it. "Most people are just sheep." Never mind the inner nature of reality, they never even thought about what the *middos* should be, or whether what they are doing is really right.

sensitivity.publishable: So when did they think it through, to arrive at the axiom? Most people didn't. It was given to them; they just got it, and followed. Never mind the inner nature of reality, they never even thought about what the *middos* should be, or whether what they are doing is really right.

blocks.text: The inner level is what *Avraham Avinu* (Abraham our father) did. He didn't just think whether it should be *chesed* or *gevura*; he thought, wait a minute, what's really going on here? That was his analysis, and that is the *pnimiyus* of *bina*.

blocks.title: Which depth is the fiftieth gate
blocks.text: Chapter one says the *omek hamusag* (the depth of the concept) is called the *shaar hanun* (the fiftieth gate), and that is not exactly what it means. *Bina sheb'bina* is called the *shaar hanun*, and so is the *omek hamusag*; it depends which. Where the depth is only understanding the explanation, it is just *omek hamusag*. *Bina sheb'bina* is a *kli* (vessel) for the depth, and it becomes the *shaar hanun* where, as with *Avraham Avinu*, it goes past the depth of *bina*, past the depth of *chachma*, to the depth of *Atik* and higher, to *Radla*, and, as chapter one says, all the way up to Him, blessed be He, *mamash*.

Most people don't do that. Their whole *hisbonenus* is analyzing external things, so though it has some of the power of *bina sheb'bina*, it is not its inner side: the whole thing is just *Nehi*. From there come the *mochin* of *Zeir Anpin*, whose *middos* are called the seven days of the week.

sections.title: Two unions: for their own sake, and for new middos
sections.summary: *Abba* and *Ima* unite either inwardly, for their own sake, in the three heads beyond the *middos*, or outwardly, in *Nehi* alone, to give *Zeir Anpin* new *mochin*. The inner union comes through the *mesirus nefesh* of the Shema, and the same split runs between the upper and the lower *Abba* and *Ima*.

phrases.he: וידוע פרטי עניני יחודים דאבא ואמא
בין כשהוא בבחינת הפנימית לצורך עצמן, שהוא בבחינת ג׳ ראשין שבהן קודם שמתפשטים במדות עדיין כו',
ובין כשמתייחדים לצורך מוחין חדשים לזעיר אנפין ונוקבה, שהוא בבחינת נה''י לבד כו'
וזהו ההפרש בין שבת לחול כו'

blocks.text: The particulars of the unions of *Abba* and *Ima* are known. The inner one is for their own sake, not for the *middos* at all. It is the *sechel* itself, and really not even the *sechel* but its depth, the inner side of *Atik*: their *gimmel reishin* (three heads), before the *middos* spread.

Yet on that level all the *middos* come out automatically, and perfectly right. That is where the real *middos* of holiness come from, because that is the real *avoda* (divine service): the inner side of *hisbonenus*.

The other union is for new *mochin* for *Zeir Anpin* and *Nukva*, in *Nehi* alone: the *middos* of what to do now or how to feel now need a *sechel*, and that comes from the outer union of *chachma* and *bina*. This is the difference between Shabbos and the weekday.

phrases.he: (ובקריאת שמע הכוונה ביהו״ה אלהינ״ו, היינו בפנימית דאבא ואמא,
phrases.en: *Havaya* is *chachma*, *Elokeinu* *bina*

phrases.he: שמשם יהו״ה אחד, יחוד דזעיר אנפין ונוקבא
כשבא להם בחינת תוספת מוחין חדשים כדי שיוכלו להוליד כו'
phrases.en: a *tosefes* of new *mochin*, in order to be able to give a *holada* to new *middos*

phrases.he: והיינו במסירת נפש דקריאת שמע,
מה שאין כן בתורה ומצות בלא מסירת נפש אין היחוד רק בחיצוניות דאבא ואמא בזעיר אנפין ונוקבה, כמו שכתוב במקום אחר
וכמו בענין עשרה הרוגי מלוכה שהעלו מיין נוקבין לאבא ואמא בבחינת הפנימית על ידי מסירת נפש דוקא)

blocks.text: In the Shema the intention in *Havaya Elokeinu* is the inner side of *Abba* and *Ima*: *Havaya* is *chachma*, *Elokeinu* is *bina*. From there comes *Havaya Echad*, the union of *Zeir Anpin* and *Nukva*, when **a *tosefes* of new *mochin*** (an addition) comes in, from the *mazalos* of the last chapter, so they can give birth to new *middos*. Otherwise it is the same old *middos*, and he is just figuring out what to do with them.

This is the *mesirus nefesh* (self-sacrifice) of the Shema. The real *hisbonenus* is *mesirus nefesh* into the *Atzmus* (G-d's essence): that is what *bina sheb'bina* is for, and that is the *shaar hanun*.

blocks.question: How can the Talmud be called an outer thing, when it is really an inner thing, called iyun, and iyun is hisbonenus?
blocks.text: Then it is what the text calls "Torah and mitzvos without *mesirus nefesh*", whose union is only in the outer side.

Studied with *mesirus nefesh* to the *Atzmus*, the *Talmud* is as the *Tanya* says: when Reuven claims this and Shimon that, the *Aibershter* says the *psak* (ruling) is such, even if it never happened and never will. That is *mamash* His *chachma*, and one who studies so gets it. That is *mesirus nefesh*, not the outer side: what to do in a certain case.

phrases.he: (וזהו ענין יחוד אבא ואמא עילאין ויחוד אבא ואמא תתאין, שהוא ישראל סבא ותבונה, כמו שכתוב למעלה בענין בינה ותבונה באריכות
ובחינת ישראל סבא הוא ו׳ קצוות דאבא ותבונה ו׳ קצוות דאימא
שנקרא אבא ואמא תתאין
ויש עוד ישראל סבא למעלה גם מאבא ואמא עילאין
phrases.en: There's really a *Yisroel Saba* and *tevuna* that go even higher than the *chachma* and *bina*

phrases.he: שהוא ו׳ קצוות דחכמה סתימאה דאריך אנפין
ותבונה ו׳ קצוות דבינה דאריך אנפין
שמשם נמשך שורש יחוד אבא ואמא עלאין בבחינת ג׳ ראשין שבהן כו')

blocks.text: This is the union of the upper *Abba* and *Ima* and of the lower, *Yisroel Saba* and *tevuna*. The upper is the very essence of the *mochin* for their own sake, which means for what is higher than *mochin*. The main thing of *Yisroel Saba* and *tevuna*, the *vav ketzavos* of *Abba* and of *Ima*, is to come up with the *middos*, though there is a *shaar hanun* in *tevuna* too.

**There's really a *Yisroel Saba* and *tevuna* that go even higher than the *chachma* and *bina***: those of *Arich*, the *vav ketzavos* of its *chachma stima'a* and of its *bina*. From there the root of the upper union, in its three heads, is drawn.

That is what was said in the last chapter: the inner union of *Abba* and *Ima* comes from the *mazalos*, *chachma stima'a* and *bina stima'a*. It has to, because *chachma* and *bina* are always into themselves, while *Yisroel Saba* and *tevuna* spread outward; *tevuna* is the spreading of the light of *bina*. So the light of *chachma* and *bina* of *Arich* spreads into those of *Atzilus* through the lower *Abba* and *Ima*.

sections.title: New souls need the inner union, and so does Moshiach
sections.summary: To bring out new souls, *Abba* and *Ima* must unite at their root, in the *mazalos* of *Arich*. This is *Kel Elyon* who "remembers the kindnesses of the fathers and brings a redeemer": the coming of Moshiach depends on *hisbonenus*.

phrases.he: והנה כאשר נמשך מאבא ואמא מוחין לזעיר אנפין ונוקבה בשביל תולדות הנשמות,
phrases.en: to have a new *tolda*

phrases.he: צריך להיות היחוד באבא ואמא בפנימית המוחין, בשרשם בב' מזלות דאריך אנפין
(והיינו בני כו' במזלא תליה כו')

blocks.text: When *Abba* and *Ima* draw *mochin* to *Zeir Anpin* and *Nukva* for the birth of souls, **to have a new *tolda*** (offspring), the union must be the inner one, receiving from their root in the two *mazalos* of *Arich*, as the last chapter said: its three levels correspond to the three levels of this chapter.
This is "children... depend on *mazal*." Even the birth of the *middos* comes back to the *mazal*.
By the way, the physical union is like that too: it has to reach the inner delight. If it does not, nothing comes out of the brains to make a new person.

sensitivity.reason: A remark on physical conception that a reader could take as a medical claim, and intimate in subject.
sensitivity.publishable: By the way, it is like that below as well: a birth has to come from the inner delight.
sensitivity.judgmentNote: It is the standard parallel between the union above and below, said briefly and modestly; weigh whether it prints as said.

phrases.he: כמו שכתוב במקום אחר שזהו ענין אל עליון, עליית אור פנימית אבא כשמקבל ממזל ונוצר כו'
אז גומל חסדים טובים,
phrases.en: when he goes up, then he can be *gomel chasadim tovim*

phrases.he: בבחינת יסוד שנקרא קונה הכל,
להוליד תולדות בזעיר אנפין ונוקבה
וזהו וזוכר חסדי אבות ומביא גואל לבני בניהם כו'
phrases.en: to remember the *chasadim* of the *Avos*, and to bring the *Moshiach*

blocks.text: As explained elsewhere, this is *Kel Elyon* (G-d most high): the ascent of the inner light of *Abba* when it receives from the *mazal* of *v'notzer*. It is the blessing in the *Shemoneh Esrei*, *Kel Elyon gomel chasadim tovim v'koneh hakol*. **When he goes up, then he can be *gomel chasadim tovim***, in *yesod*, called *koneh hakol*, and *Zeir Anpin* and *Nukva* can give birth.

This is *v'zocher chasdei avos umevi go'el*: **to remember the *chasadim* of the *Avos*, and to bring the *Moshiach***, there has to be an inner union of *Abba*, *hisbonenus davka*. It is not so obvious, but that is what he is saying.

Moshiach will not come the way people think, somehow, from this or from that: without an inner union there are no offspring, and there can't be a Moshiach. More than that: the whole real thing of Moshiach is this.

sections.title: The mashal: only a sage who knows the source can teach a child
sections.summary: A wondrous sage who knows an idea at its source can recast it for a small child and bring new ideas out of it; one who only grasps it as it is can do neither. So the giving power of *chachma*, its *yesod*, depends on the source of the intellect.

phrases.he: והמשל בזה ידוע,
phrases.en: and the *mashal* of this is known

phrases.he: כמו איש שהוא חכם מופלג ביותר,
phrases.en: a super smart guy

phrases.he: כאשר יודע לעומק השכל ממקור חוצבו דוקא,
phrases.en: when he knows the *omek hasechel*, not just that he heard an explanation, but in its inner quarry where it's coming from

phrases.he: אז יכול להיות משפיע לנמוך ביותר,
phrases.en: then he can explain it to the lowest person

phrases.he: גם לתינוק קטן
לעשות צירופים חדשים באופן השכלת השכל ההוא,
phrases.en: Then he can make new *tzirufim* in how to be *maskil* this *sechel* to somebody else

phrases.he: לא כהוויתו דוקא
phrases.en: he can come up with a whole new different explanation that will make sense to this lower guy

phrases.he: וכן ביכולתו לחדש שכל אחר, להוליד מחדש מחמת זה השכל
phrases.en: he can be *mechadesh* a whole new *sechel*, to bring into a birth of a new *sechel* from this *sechel*

blocks.title: The great sage and the small child
blocks.text: The *mashal* is known: **a super smart guy**, who knows the depth of an idea not because he heard an explanation but **in its inner quarry where it's coming from**, can **explain it to the lowest person**, even a small child. He can make new *tzirufim* (combinations) of it: **a whole new different explanation that will make sense to this lower guy**. That is a whole *tolda*.
More than that, he can **be *mechadesh* a whole new *sechel***: from this idea, the birth of a new one. That happens only when there is an inner union of the *mochin*.

phrases.he: מה שאין כן מי שאינו חכם מופלג ואינו תופס רק החכמה והשכל דברים כהוויתן לבד
די להפקיע להשיגו לעצמו בלבד
phrases.en: just that he understands it for himself: he understood the explanation

phrases.he: אבל לא יוכל להוליד חדשות ממנו כלל
phrases.en: but he won't be able to bring new things out of it

phrases.he: וכל שכן שלא יוכל להוליד ולהשפיל הסבר השכל להבינו לתינוק כו'
ונמצא שבחינת נה''י דחכמה, שהוא בחינת יסוד, הכח המשפיע למקבל, תלוי בכח המשכיל, מקור חוצב השכל מאין ליש דוקא כו'

blocks.text: Not so one who is not a *chacham muflag* (a wondrous sage) and grasps things only as they are, **just that he understands it for himself**: **but he won't be able to bring new things out of it**, still less bring the explanation down to a child. So the *Nehi* of *chachma*, *yesod*, the power that gives to a receiver, depends on the power of the *maskil*, the quarry of the intellect, from *ayin* to *yesh davka*.

blocks.question: You just said Nehi is only the outer side of the intellect; now it depends on the source?
blocks.text: That is the outer *Nehi*: bringing a little light over into the *middos*, not giving birth to new *middos*. To bring the actual drop from the *sechel* over into an actual *tolda*, really giving to somebody else, you need a *chacham muflag* who reaches all the way into the inner side of the *sechel*, from *ayin* to *yesh davka*.

sections.title: The nimshal: souls, and the union of Friday night
sections.summary: Souls are born only with added power from far above the intellect, from the *mazalos* of *chachma stima'a*. That is why the inner union of *Abba* and *Ima* is on Friday night, the time of the union of the wise.

phrases.he: וכך הוא בענין תולדות הנשמות מבחינת נה''י
שאינו מוליד כי אם בתוספת כח במקור המוחין שלו
מלמעלה מעלה מן השכל כו'
phrases.en: It has to go all the way to the source of the *taanug*

phrases.he: והוא הטעם שבשביל תולדות נשמות על ידי יחוד אבא ואמא, צריך להיות מלמעלה ממקור המוחין דאבא ואמא שזהו מבחינת מזלות דחכמה סתימאה שהוא למעלה גם מחכמה ובינה דאריך אנפין עצמו כנזכר לעיל

והיינו טעם ליחוד פנימית דאבא ואמא בליל שבת קודש מפני שהוא בשביל להוליד נשמות שלכך אז דוקא זמן זיווגא דחכימין שהן תלמידי חכמים שנקרא קודש, ושבת שרשו בקודש העליון, בחינת פנימית אור אבא כנזכר לעיל ודי למבין:

blocks.text: So with the birth of souls from the *Nehi* of *Zeir Anpin*: they are born only with added power from the source of its *mochin*, far above the intellect. **It has to go all the way to the source of the *taanug***. That is why, for souls to be born of the union of *Abba* and *Ima*, it must be drawn from above the source of their *mochin*: from the *mazalos* of *chachma stima'a*, above even *chachma* and *bina* of *Arich*. It really comes from *Atik*.

That is the reason for the inner union of *Abba* and *Ima* on Friday night: it is to give birth to souls. So it is *davka* the time of the union of the wise, the Torah scholars, who are called holy; and Shabbos is rooted in the upper holiness, the inner light of *Abba*.

reviewQuestions.question: What are the three levels of *chachma*, and which of them does most people's day-to-day thinking come from?
Why is the analysis of the *Talmud*, guilty or innocent, usually the outer side of *chachma* and *bina*, and when is it the inner side?
What is a *hanacha sichlis*, and what do the whales show about how most people think?
Why does the coming of Moshiach depend on the inner union, that is, on *hisbonenus*?
In the *mashal*, what can the wondrous sage do that one who grasps an idea only as it is cannot, and why?

omitted.note: Lines 1-4 read at the opening of the side with no English and no comment (w0-2 is the first words of line 1, cut off).
He finishes reading line 32 and reads line 33 (the ten martyrs) with no comment; the transcript garbles line 33.

notes.text: The whole chapter is one class (040), which reads every line in order and ends with the last line of the chapter. Lines 1-4 are read with no English or comment: the passage is skip read-only, its words in omitted as reading.

040 w1619-1639: "Most people didn't, it was just a חשמל in the first place. Like we're going to learn later about חשמל." The word may be misheard and I could not tell what he meant by it here, so the aside on people's axioms leaves it out.

040 w1903-1929: "all the way up to מגלוי ונעלם דכולא ברוך הוא ממש" is garbled (perhaps a phrase like "the hidden of all hidden" from chapter one). The digression says only "all the way up to Him, blessed be He, mamash".
040 w566-573: "Like how רב ליוויק would learn the תלמוד": presumably Reb Levi Yitzchak Schneerson, the Rebbe's father; kept as "Reb Levik", as he said it.

040 w2373-2433: "like it says in Tanya, I think it was just today, yesterday": the Reuven and Shimon example of a ruling as G-d's wisdom is presumably Tanya chapter 5; the block keeps "the Tanya" only.
In line 21 the transcript has him read "ההלכות" / "ההלכה" where the text has "השכלות" (w890-906, w936-943); probably misheard. The block follows the chapter text.
The "intellectual axiom" (w1437-1447) may be a student's suggestion, answering his asking for the English word; the block gives it without saying who.

Several phrases carry his gloss rather than a word-for-word rendering, because that is the English he gives there: line 25 ("He's a wishy-washy guy..."), line 26 ("That's also the strength of the bina"), line 54 ("It has to go all the way to the source of the taanug"), line 46 ("he can come up with a whole new different explanation").

The question at w3482-3503 ("So, what do you mean? You just told me that Nehi is just the outer side") is marked askedBy teacher: it reads as him putting the objection to the text ("He says, yeah..."), but it could be a student's.
Lines 53-60 are one passage: he reads them straight through in the last minute of the side, with two short remarks (w3598-3612, w3641-3645).
